answer: Reciprocal Neighbor Beaconing. Each agent emits a periodic beacon naming its active counterparties; an agent counts as reachable only while its neighbors cite it back within a rolling window. Forgery fails because false reciprocity must be sustained by real message traffic, not one-time records—every fake identity needs a live counterparty also spending bandwidth and storage. Honest clusters form an oasis of mutually confirmed nodes, while a sudden tide of uncited newcomers is throttled to low-priority relay. Attack cost scales with maintaining bidirectional traffic for each sock puppet.
